title: Partial algebraization of a complete normal strictly local scheme
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime and let $X$ be a normal complete strictly henselian local Noetherian excellent scheme of finite Krull dimension $d\geq2$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Complete means complete for its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]; normal means its local rings are integrally closed domains. There exist a finite surjective morphism $p:X\prime\to X$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], with $X\prime$ normal, a complete regular local Noetherian excellent scheme $S$ of dimension $d-1$ with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], a finite-type morphism $Z\to S$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and a geometric point $\bar z\to Z$, such that $$X\prime\cong\widehat{Z_{(\bar z)}}.$$ Here $Z_{(\bar z)}$ is strict localization [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and the hat is completion for its maximal ideal. The scheme $Z_{(\bar z)}$ is Noetherian excellent, admits a dimension function, and the completion map $X\prime\to Z_{(\bar z)}$ is regular (flat with geometrically regular fibres). In equal characteristic the finite cover may be taken to be the identity. Krull dimension is the supremum of lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

source.place: Expose V, geometric reformulation 3.1.3 and Remark 3.1.4; the strict-local form used in Expose XVII, final paragraph of 6.5, printed p. 300

proof.text: Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Apply [lem-per-cohen-gabber-finite-presentations] to obtain $A\hookrightarrow A'$, $\Lambda$, $r$, $R=\Lambda[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]\hookrightarrow A'$ and $f$ as in its statement. The normal domain $A'$ is finite over the complete Noetherian local ring $A$, hence is itself Noetherian complete local by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product]. The injection $A\to A'$ gives a finite morphism by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], hence an integral morphism by [pqf-lem-finite-integral-lft]; its map on spectra is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over]. In equal characteristic this map is the identity. Put $D=\Lambda[[t_1,\ldots,t_{r-1}]]$. The presentation lemma gives that $D$ is complete regular Noetherian local, and its dimension is $d-1$ in both cases: $r-1=d-1$ over a field, and $1+(r-1)=d-1$ over a discrete valuation ring. Its residue field is separably closed. Also $\ell$ is a unit in $D$: the residue characteristic is that of $A'$, a finite residue extension of that of $A$, and is different from $\ell$.

source.place: Expose IV 2.1.1, 4.2.2 and 4.2.5; V 2.2.2, 3.1.3 and Remark 3.1.4. Only a finite surjection, not a prime-to-ell degree, is required here.

proof.text: Replace $f$ by $f t_r$. This remains nonzero modulo $\mathfrak m_\Lambda$, belongs to $\mathfrak m_R$, and the finite map is still etale after inverting it, because that localization also inverts the original $f$. More explicitly, the open immersion of the inverse image of $D(ft_r)$ into the inverse image of $D(f)$ is etale; compose with the etale map to $D(f)$ and cancel the etale open immersion $D(ft_r)\to D(f)$, using (1)–(3) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Use [lem-per-weierstrass-henselian-cylinder] on this element. Re-express the presentation $R\to A'$ in the coordinates of that lemma (equivalently compose it with the inverse coordinate automorphism). It supplies a distinguished polynomial $g\in D[T]$, $R_0=D[T]$, $\mathfrak q=(\mathfrak m_D,T)$, and $H=(R_0)_{\mathfrak q}^{h}$ with $(H,gH)$ henselian, $H$ Noetherian, and $\widehat H_{gH}=R=\widehat H_{\mathfrak m_H}$. The map $R\to A'$ is etale away from $g$: $c(ft_r)=ug$ with $u$ a unit, so the corresponding principal open is exactly $D(g)$. This also covers mixed dimension $d=2$, where $r=1$ and there are no coordinates to change.

source.place: Expose V 1.1.1, 1.1.3, 1.2.3 and 2.2.3; the same cylinder construction applies to the mixed-characteristic presentation of IV 4.2.2.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-elkik-finite-etale-away-completion] to the Noetherian henselian pair $(H,gH)$. Its $g$-adic completion is the ring $R$ from Step 2, and the finite $R$-algebra $A'$ is etale outside $V(g)$. Thus there is a finite $H$-algebra $C$ and an $R$-algebra isomorphism $R\otimes_H C\cong A'$. No smoothness at points of $V(g)$ is assumed or used.

source.place: Expose V Theorem 1.2.4 and its application in 2.2.3.

proof.text: Use [lem-per-finite-henselian-algebra-local-model] with the Noetherian base $D$, $R_0=D[T]$, the closed point $\mathfrak q=(\mathfrak m_D,T)$, and the finite $H$-algebra $C$ of Step 3. Its residue-field hypothesis holds because $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=D/\mathfrak m_D$ is separably closed. Its completed-tensor hypothesis holds because $\widehat H_{\mathfrak m_H}=R$ and $R\otimes_H C\cong A'$ is a nonzero local domain. We obtain a Noetherian strictly henselian local ring $C$, a finite-type $D$-scheme $Z=\operatorname{Spec}F$, and a geometric closed point $\bar z$ over the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}D$, with $\operatorname{Spec}C\cong Z_{(\bar z)}$. This is the strict localization itself, not merely an ordinary local ring with the same completion.

source.place: Expose V 2.2.7, and the strict-local formulation of Expose XVII 6.5, printed p.300.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension] to the finite map $H\to C$ at $\mathfrak m_H$. Since $C$ is local, there is exactly one prime over $\mathfrak m_H$: any such prime is maximal by [pqf-lem-finite-integral-lft] and [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal], and its maximal ideal lies over $\mathfrak m_H$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical]. The completion theorem therefore identifies $\widehat H\otimes_H C$ with the maximal-ideal completion $\widehat C$, as algebras over $C$. Combining this identification with Step 3 gives $A'\cong\widehat C$. Thus $X'=\operatorname{Spec}A'\cong\widehat{Z_{(\bar z)}}$, compatibly with the canonical completion map to $Z_{(\bar z)}$.

source.place: Expose V 2.2.3 (both completion topologies) and 2.2.7; Stacks algebra.tex, Tag 07N9, lemma-completion-finite-extension.

proof.text: The base $D$ is excellent by [lem-per-complete-local-excellence]. Since $F$ is finite type over $D$, [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] makes $Z$ Noetherian excellent. Apply [lem-per-regular-strict-local-model] to the identity regular morphism $Z\to Z$ at $\bar z$: the identity is flat and has field fibres, which remain fields after extension of the residue field. That node gives that $Z_{(\bar z)}=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is Noetherian excellent. In particular $C$ is a G-ring by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Now [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-completion-regular], for the ideal $\mathfrak m_C$, says precisely that the canonical completion morphism $X'=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat C\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is flat with geometrically regular fibres.

source.place: Expose XVII, final paragraph of 6.5; Stacks more-algebra.tex, Tags 07QW (complete local excellence), 07QU (finite type and localization), and 0AH2 (regular completion of a G-ring).

proof.text: Excellence implies universal catenarity by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. The Noetherian excellent local scheme $Z_{(\bar z)}$ therefore admits a dimension function by [lem-per-local-dimension-function-calculus]. Together with Steps 1 and 5 this gives every asserted property, with $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ and the already constructed finite-type map $Z\to S$.

source.place: Expose XIV Proposition 2.1.4 and Theorem 2.2.1; Expose XVII 6.5.
